The Court made the following:
JUDGMENT:(per Hon'ble The Chief Justice Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta)
1. The dispute relating to inter se seniority between
the Direct Recruits (DRs) and the Promotees (PRs) has once
again emerged as the bone of contention between the
parties. The dispute pertains to the post of Assistant
Engineer in the Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited (for
short "UPCL").
2. The recruitment and conditions of service of
engineers in UPCL is governed by the U.P. State Electricity
2

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
Board Services of Engineers Regulations, 1970 (for short "the
Service Regulations 1970"). In terms of Regulation 5 of
thereof, the quota prescribed for DRs was 50.33% and for
PRs 49.67%, which for all practical purposes was in the ratio
of 1:1.
3. The case of the UPCL is that, for initiation of the
selection process for the year 2008-09, its HR department, on
25.08.2008, sought approval from the Managing Director for
commencing the process of direct recruitment to the post of
Assistant Engineers (E&M) along with certain other posts.
The Managing Director accorded approval on 27.09.2008.
Pursuant thereto, quotations were invited from various
recruitment agencies/ departments on 13.10.2008. On
01.11.2008, an exercise for determination of the vacancies
falling to the respective quotas of DRs and PRs was
undertaken. As per the said exercise, as on 01.11.2008, 72
vacancies were available under the direct recruitment quota
and 53 vacancies under the promotion quota.
4. Upon determination of the vacancies, the
recruitment process under both sources, namely, direct
recruitment and promotion, was commenced.
3

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
Process of Recruitment by Promotion
5. A meeting of the Departmental Promotion
Committee (DPC) meeting was held on 19.11.2008, in which
11 Junior Engineers were found suitable for promotion and,
accordingly, promotion orders were issued in their favour.
(A) Since sufficient number of eligible Junior Engineers
were not available, the qualifying period of service was
relaxed by 50% vide O.M. dated 22.01.2009, thereby
bringing more Junior Engineers within the zone of
consideration for promotion.
(B) Thereafter, another DPC was held on 30.06.2009,
and based on its recommendation, 43 more Junior Engineers
were promoted on the same day.
Process for recruitment of Assistant Engineers by
Direct Recruitment
6. On 26.02.2009, an advertisement was issued
inviting applications for direct recruitment against 68 posts of
Assistant Engineers (Trainee) (E&M). UPCL initially intended
to conclude the appointment process by 30.06.2009.
(A) The selection process, however, could not be
completed within the contemplated period and was delayed
for various reasons, including objections raised by different
associations regarding the qualifications prescribed for Junior
4

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
Engineers and other related issues. The recruitment agency
also requested for four months' time from the last date of
receipt of application for completing the recruitment process.
(B) The written examination was eventually held on
09.08.2009, followed by interviews on 23.11.2009,
26.11.2009 and 30.11.2009. As a result of the selection
process, 39 vacancies were filled, while remaining 29
vacancies falling under the DR quota were carried forward to
the next recruitment process.
(C) The DRs, who are respondent nos.3 to 40 herein,
joined as Assistant Engineers between December, 2009 and
January, 2010.
The Dispute
7. The dispute between the PRs and DRs relates to
their respective placement in the seniority list. The seniority
of the employees of the Corporation is regulated by the U.P.
State Electricity Board Employees Seniority Regulations, 1998
(for short "the Seniority Regulations, 1998"). The case of the
DRs is that the vacancies against which both sets of
employees were recruited pertained to the same recruitment
year 2008-09, and that the recruitment through both sources
formed part of one composite recruitment exercise, i.e. "one
selection" and, therefore, in view of Regulation 8 of the
5

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
Seniority Regulations, 1998 read with other applicable
regulations, and applying the quota, as prescribed under
Regulation 5 of the Service Regulations, 1970, they were
liable to be interspaced in the seniority list in the ratio of 1:1
notwithstanding the fact that they actually joined services at
a later point of time. It is further contended on behalf of the
DRs' that the delay in completing the direct recruitment
process of DRs' for reasons beyond their control cannot
operate to their prejudice in the matter of seniority.
According to them, recruitment from both the sources having
been initiated against vacancies of the same recruitment
year, the mere fact that the direct recruitment process took
longer time to conclude would not disentitle them to their
placement according to the prescribed rota quota. Any other
interpretation, according to them, would render the rota
quota principle contemplated under the Seniority Regulations,
1998, otiose.
8. The PRs, on the other hand, contended that the
DRs came to be appointed only during the next recruitment
year 2009-10 and, therefore, cannot claim placement in the
seniority list pertaining to the recruitment year 2008-09.
According to them, giving such placement to the DRs would
amount to assigning seniority to them from a date anterior to
6

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
their entry into the cadre, contrary to the settled principle of
service jurisprudence that an employee cannot ordinarily be
given seniority from a date when he was not even borne on
the cadre. Their further contention is that the recruitment of
DR's and PR's was not the outcome of "one selection" and,
therefore, Regulation 8(3) of the Seniority Regulations, 1998
which mandate fixation of seniority of DR's and PR's on basis
of result of "any one selection" in a cyclic order, would not
apply.
Relevant Details of Past Litigation
9. On 03.01.2015, UPCL published a combined
seniority list of the Assistant Engineers, in which, the DRs'
were given seniority from the date they joined the services as
"Trainee", after their selection on basis of the advertisement.
Aggrieved by the said seniority list, eight Assistant Engineers
(PRs) challenged the seniority list in Claim Petition
No.01/NB/DB/2015 before the Uttarakhand Public Services
Tribunal, Bench at Nainital (for short "the Tribunal"). The
case of the PRs was that the DRs' were wrongly given
seniority from the date of their induction as "Trainees".
According to the PRs', the DRs' were entitled to seniority from
the date of their substantive appointment in the cadre after
completion of their training.
7

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
10. The claim petition was allowed by the Tribunal by
order dated 07.11.2017 and it was held that the training
period was liable to be excluded for the purposes of seniority.
Accordingly, the UPCL was directed to prepare a fresh
seniority list by treating the appointment of DRs' from the
date of their substantive appointment to the cadre after
completion of their training period.
11. The order of the Tribunal was challenged before
this Court by the UPCL as well as DRs' in a batch of writ
petitions [Writ Petition (S/B) No.579 of 2017,
Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd. vs. Shri B.M. Bhatt
& others and other connected writ petitions].
12. By common judgment dated 27.06.2024, the writ
petitions were allowed giving seniority to the DRs, who joined
in the years 2006-07, 2007-08 and 2008-09 from the date of
their joining the Department holding that the training period
was part of the regular service. The relevant findings and the
operative part of the judgment dated 27.06.2024 is as
follows:-
"20. Since, in the facts of the present case, as per the Office
Memorandum dated 31.03.2001 - Annexure 4, till the new
regulations were framed, the Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd.
was to follow the Regulations of 1970 and 1998 of the U.P. Power
Corporation Ltd. for the purpose of recruitment and fixation of
8

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
seniority. It is not the case of the respondents that any new
Regulations have been framed by the Uttarakhand Power
Corporation Ltd. Hence, for all intents and purposes, as per the
Office Memorandum dated 31.03.2001, the seniority Rules of the
U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., i.e. the 1970 Regulations and 1998
Regulations, have to be followed, and the Rule of seniority, which is
Rule 19 reproduced above, is very clear that the seniority has to be
fixed from the date a selected candidate joins on the post. Hence,
for all intents and purposes, the training period cannot be deleted
once an Assistant Engineer, after due selection process, has joined
the cadre.
21. Another fact, which can be highlighted, is that even if
during service any employee is sent for further training, that period
cannot be deleted from his seniority. It is part of his service, and at
the initial stage if he is given training, or even after ten years he is
sent for training, that period of training has to be part of his regular
service record.
22. In view of the above discussion, the present Writ Petitions
are being allowed. The order of the Tribunal is being set-aside. A
direction is being given to the Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd.
to fix the seniority after giving the benefit of seniority to all the
Assistant Engineers, who joined in the year 2006-07, 2007-08 &
2008-09 from the date of their joining the department, and keeping
in view the rota quota between the direct recruits and the
promotees. The entire exercise shall be completed with a period of
eight weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this
judgment."
(emphasis supplied)
13. The dispute before the Tribunal as well as in the
writ petitions was only with regard to the training period of
the DRs. It was only the said controversy which was decided
by the Tribunal as well as by this Court and, therefore, in
respect thereof only, a direction was issued for fixation of
seniority of the DRs from the date of their joining the
9

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
Department. However, according to UPCL, the observation
that the seniority be fixed keeping in view the rota-quota
between the DR's and PR's led to confusion regarding the
applicability of the rota-quota rule. Consequently, two
clarification applications, being MCC Nos.19229 and 19230 of
2024, were filed before the Court seeking clarification of the
judgment dated 27.06.2024.
14. The aforesaid applications were disposed of by this
Court by issuing the following clarification vide order dated
14.02.2025:-
"11. This Court had in clear terms given direction as to what
this Court has decided and this has been so stated in para 22 of the
judgment. With regard to rota quota as such no direction has been
made. The Court has simply stated ".....and keeping in view the
rota quota between the direct recruits and the promotees."
12. This Court only intends to clarify that rota quota shall be
given in accordance with the existing statutory rules/ regulations."
15. Thus, this Court clarified that its direction contained
in Para 22 of the judgment should not be read as altering the
principle of rota-quota but rather the direction was to prepare
the seniority list keeping in view the said Rule.
Stand of UPCL:-
16. In order to resolve the aforesaid dispute and
pursuant to the order dated 27.06.2024 passed in Writ
Petition (S/B) No.579 of 2017 and other connected writ
10

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
petitions, the UPCL constituted a High Level Committee
comprising of Shri Lalit Mohan Rayal, IAS, Additional
Secretary (Personnel and Vigilance), Government of
Uttarakhand, Dr. Ahmed Iqbal, IAS, Additional Secretary
(Energy), Government of Uttarakhand and Mr. Sudhir Kumar,
HJS, Additional Secretary (Law), Government of Uttarakhand.
(A) The said Committee submitted its report dated
17.04.2025 and it recommended that a combined select list
be prepared keeping the PRs at the first place and DRs at the
second place and so on. It also recommended that DRs, who
were appointed in pursuance of the advertisement issued in
February, 2009 and who joined in December 2009 onwards
be amalgamated with the PRs of 2008-09 by applying rota
quota rule of 1:1, as envisaged in Regulation 8(3) of the
Seniority Regulations, 1998.
(B) On 15.05.2025, the UPCL forwarded the report of High-Level Committee to the Chief Secretary-cum-Chairman,
UPCL, Government of Uttarakhand. On 04.06.2025, an office
memorandum was issued publishing a combined seniority list
of Assistant Engineers (E&M) of the year 2008-09, in which,
the DR's were interspaced with the PR's.
11

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
Analysis
17. Initially, the inter se seniority between PRs and DRs
was governed by the fourth proviso to Regulation 19 of the
Service Regulations, 1970, which read as follows:-
"Rule 19
Seniority.......
Provided fourthly that as between candidates who are
appointed by direct recruitment and who are recruited by
promotion in the same year, the seniority shall be
determined in the order in which their names are arranged
in the combined waiting list prepared under Regulation 15,
provided that if in any year, it has not been possible to
prepare the combined waiting list due to late selection either
from Junior Engineers Service or from Computers (Selection
Grade) or found outside or due to any other unavoidable
reasons, the names in the gradation list shall be arranged in
the same order in due course in respect of the vacancies
allotted to each of the categories of candidates in that
particular year, as in the combined waiting list and the
seniority determined accordingly."
18. However, after the promulgation of the U.P. State
Electricity Board Employees Seniority Regulations, 1998, the
matter of seniority came to be governed by these
Regulations, which, in view of Regulation 3 thereof, prevails
over anything to the contrary contained in the Service
Regulations. Regulation 3 of the Seniority Regulations reads
thus:-
"3. Overriding Effect:-
These regulations shall have effect notwithstanding anything
to the contrary contained in any other service regulations made
heretobefore."
12

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
19. Regulation 4 of the Seniority Regulations is the
definition clause. Some of the expressions defined therein,
which are relevant to the controversy, are as follows:-
"4(b) "Cadre" means the strength of the service, or part of
the service sanctioned as a separate unit.
4(h) "substantive appointment" means an appointment not
being an adhoc appointment on a post in the cadre of the service
made after selection in accordance with the service regulations
relating to that service.
4(i) "year" means one period of twelve months starting from
1st day of July".
20. Seniority Regulation 5 deals with seniority where
appointments are to be made by direct recruitment only.
Though, it is not directly applicable to the present dispute,
but it uses certain expressions which would be helpful in
interpreting the applicable Regulations, and is therefore
reproduced below:-
"5. Seniority where appointments are to be made by direct
recruitment only:
Where according to the service regulations appointments are
to be made only by the direct recruitment the seniority inter-se of
the persons appointed on the result of any one selection shall be
the same as it is shown in the merit list prepared by the
commission, or the committee as the case may be;
Provided that a candidate recruited directly may lose his seniority,
if he fails to join without valid reasons when vacancy is offered to
him, the decision of the appointing authority as to the validity of
reasons shall be final;
Provided further that the persons appointed on the result of a
subsequent selection shall be junior to the persons appointed on
the result of a previous selection;
13

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
Explanation: Where in the same year separate selections for
regular and emergency recruitment are made the selections for
regular recruitment shall be deemed to be the previous selection."
21. Regulation 6 of the Seniority Regulations deals with
seniority where appointments are to be made by promotion
only from a single feeding cadre, whereas Regulation 7 deals
with cases where promotions are made from several feeding
cadres. Regulation 8 of the Seniority Regulations is the
relevant provision governing the inter-se seniority between
PRs and DRs, where appointments are made both by
promotion and direct recruitment, as in the present case.
Regulation 8 is as follows:-
"8. Seniority where appointments are made by promotion and
direct recruitment:
(1) Where according to the service regulations appointments
are made both by promotion and by direct recruitment, the
seniority of persons appointed shall, subject to the
provisions of the following sub-regulations, be
determined from the date of the order of their substantive
appointment and if two or more persons are appointed
together, in the order in which their names are arranged in
the appointment order:
Provided that if the appointment order specifies a particular
backdate with effect from which a person is substantively
appointed, that date will be deemed to be the date of order
of substantive appointment and, in other cases, it will mean
the date of issuance of the order.
Provided further that a candidate recruited directly may lose
his seniority if he fails to join without valid reasons when
vacancy is offered to him, the decision of the appointing
authority as to the validity of reasons shall be final.
14

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
(2) The seniority inter-se of persons appointed on the result
of any one selection:
(a) through direct recruitment shall be the same as it
is shown in the merit list prepared by the Commission
or by the Committee, as the case may be;
(b) by promotion shall be as determined in
accordance with the principles laid down in Regulation
6 or Regulation 7, as the case may be, according as
the promotions are to be made from a single feeding
cadre or several feeding cadres;
(3) Where appointments are made both by promotion and
direct recruitment as a result of any one selection the
seniority of promotes vis-à-vis direct recruits shall be
determined in a cyclic order (the first being a promotee) so
far as may be in accordance with the quota prescribed for
the two sources.
Illustrations:
(1) Where the quota of promotes and direct recruits is in the
proportion of 1:1, the seniority shall be in the following
order:
First---------Promotee
Second------Direct Recruit
and so on.
(2) Where the said quota is in the proportion of 1:3, the
seniority shall be in the following order:
First-----Promotee
Second to Fourth------Direct Recruits
Fifth-------Promotee
Sixth to Eighth------Direct Recruits
and so on.
Provided that:
(i) Where appointments from any source are made in excess
of the prescribed quota, the persons appointed in excess of
quota shall be pushed down for seniority to subsequent year
or years in which there are vacancies in accordance with the
quota.
(ii) Where appointments from any source fall short of the
prescribed quota and appointments against such unfilled
vacancies are made in subsequent year or years, the
persons so appointed shall not get seniority of any earlier
15

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
year but shall get the seniority of the year in which their
appointments are made so however that their names shall
be placed at the top followed by the names in the cyclic
order of the other appointees.
(iii) Where, in accordance with the service regulations, the
unfilled vacancies from any source could in the
circumstances mentioned in the relevant service regulations
be filled from the other source and appointments in excess
of quota are so made, the persons so appointed shall get the
seniority of that very year as if they are appointed against
the vacancies of their quota."
22. According to Mr. Shobhit Saharia, learned counsel
for the promotees, the seniority has to be determined from
the date of the order of substantive appointment, as
stipulated under Regulation 8(1). It is contended that
seniority cannot be given to the DRs from any date anterior
to the date of their substantive appointment, otherwise, it
would be violative of Regulation 8(1).
23. Elaborating his submission, he submits that this
would be further clear from the definition of "substantive
appointment" under Regulation 4(h), which defines the
phrase to mean an appointment after selection in accordance
with the Service Regulations. This, in case of DRs happened
when the select list of 55 candidates was issued on
07.12.2009, followed by their appointments from December,
2009 onwards. On the other hand, the selection process of
the PRs got concluded with the holding of the second DPC on
16

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
30.06.2008 and their joining on the promoted posts on the
same date, when the selection process in respect of DRs was
still in progress. Therefore, the DRs cannot be inter-spaced
with PRs in the seniority list, otherwise it would be violative of
the criteria laid down for determining seniority under
Regulation 8(1) of the Seniority Regulations.
24. On the other hand, Mr. Arunabh Chowdhury,
learned Senior Counsel appearing for the UPCL submitted that
Regulation 8(3) specifically uses the expression "result of any
one selection" and not "selection in one year" or "selection in
one recruitment year". Consequently, a selection does not
cease to be "one selection" merely because its different
components are completed in different recruitment years.
Reliance in this regard was placed upon Coordinate Bench
judgments of this Court in "Rakesh Nautiyal vs. State of
Uttarakhand & another", 2010 SCC OnLine Utt 2757 and
Dr. Sunita Pandey vs. State of Uttarakhand, [Writ
Petition (S/B) No.297 of 2017], dated 21.07.2020, as also
upon Amit Singh vs. Ravindra Nath Pandey, (2022) 20
SCC 559, where a pari materia provision was considered.
25. It is further contended that the Seniority
Regulations, 1998 uses three distinct phrases of selection,
17

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
namely, "any one selection" in Regulation 8(2), Regulation
8(3) and Regulation 5; "subsequent selection" in second
proviso to Regulation 5 and the second proviso Regulation 7
and, "separate selection" in explanation to Regulation 5.
26. The contention is that the phrase "one selection"
has been deliberately used in Regulation 8(3) as distinguished
with "subsequent selection" and "separate selection". Thus,
'the result of any one selection' appearing in Regulation 8(3)
where appointments are made both by promotion and direct
recruitment refers to conclusion of selection process with the
appointment of both promotes and direct recruits.
27. According to UPCL, the recruitment of Assistant
Engineers for the selection year 2008-09 was a composite
exercise involving two sources- promotion and direct
recruitment. Vacancies under both quotas had been
identified and the direct recruitment process was initiated for
the vacancies pertaining to that selection year. The
advertisement dated 26.02.2009 was issued for filling the
direct recruitment quota. Although the DRs ultimately came
to be appointed in December, 2009 and January, 2010, the
delay was attributable to administrative reasons and
objections raised during the recruitment process and not to
18

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
any fault on their part. Accordingly, it is contended that
subsequent appointment of DRs did not make their
recruitment a separate selection for the purposes of
Regulation 8(3). Once appointments from both sources were
the result of the same selection, the UPCL was obliged to
integrate them and determine their inter se seniority in the
prescribed 1:1 cyclic order, consistent with the quota
between PRs and DRs.
28. Reliance has been placed on the Constitution Bench
judgment of the Supreme Court in Mervyn Coutindo and
Others vs. Collector of Customs, Bombay & others, AIR
1967 SC 52; Union of India & others vs. S.D. Gupta &
others, (1996) 8 SCC 14 and M. Subba Reddy & another
vs. A.P. State Road Transport Corporation & others,
(2004) 6 SCC 729 in support of the proposition that where
the governing rules prescribe rota-quota, administrative delay
in recruitment from one source cannot defeat the statutory
arrangement.
29. Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned Senior Counsel
appearing for the DRs submitted that Regulations 15 and 17
of the Service Regulations contemplate preparation of a
combined waiting list before appointments are made.
19

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
According to learned Senior Counsel, the Corporation, instead
of awaiting completion of the direct recruitment process and
preparing such combined waiting list, issued promotion orders
of 43 Junior Engineers on 30.06.2009 itself. The omission on
part of the Corporation to follow the prescribed procedure, it
was urged, cannot operate to the prejudice of the DRs.
30. It is further contended that amended Regulation 5,
which permits recruitment and promotion proceedings from
different categories to be undertaken separately, does not
dispense with the requirement of Regulations 15 and 17. The
separate modes of selection, according to him, ultimately
converge for the purpose of preparing the combined waiting
list and determining inter se seniority.
31. Lastly, relying upon Jamil Ahmed vs. Industrial
Development Commissioner and Principal Secretary,
(2004) 13 SCC 736 and Union of India vs. Smt. Sadhana
Khanna, (2008) 1 SCC 720, it was submitted that the DRs
cannot be made to suffer on account of delay or failure
attributable to the Corporation in completing the recruitment
process or in complying with the applicable Regulations.
32. Apart from the aforesaid judgments, Mr. Bahuguna,
learned Senior Counsel has also placed reliance on the
20

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
judgments cited by learned Senior Counsel appearing for the
UPCL to buttress his submission that where governing rules
make applicable rota-quota, seniority has to be determined
on basis thereof and mere delay in completing the process of
recruitment from any particular source would not operate to
the prejudice of the persons recruited through the said
source.
33. A close reading of Regulation 8 of the Seniority
Regulations reveals that sub-regulation (1) thereof lays down
general principle for determining seniority, namely, that the
seniority is to be determined from "the date of the order of
substantive appointment", and when two or more persons are
appointed together, in the order in which their names are
arranged in the appointment order. Notably, the provision
itself enumerates some of the situations when seniority is not
to be determined from "the date of the order of substantive
appointment", but from a different date. Thus, where the
order of appointment specifies a particular backdate, seniority
has to be reckoned from the date stipulated in the order of
appointment and not from the date of the order of
substantive appointment. Another such situation is envisaged
under the second proviso to sub-regulation (1), where if there
is delay in joining without valid reason, seniority of such a
21

UKHC010089962025
2026:UHC:8277-DB
candidate is counted from the date of joining and not from
the date of order of appointment. Another, noteworthy
aspect is that sub-regulation (1) is subject to the provision of
"the following sub-regulations", namely, sub-regulations (2)
and (3). Thus, the mode of determination of seniority
envisaged under sub-regulations (2) and (3) would prevail
over sub-regulation (1).
34. Sub-regulation (2) of Regulation 8 of the Seniority
